claim: For exact-50/50 binary queries, max C_F is 1 at n=2, 2 at n=4, and n-3 for every even n>=6.

upper_bound_certificate.step_1: Every query in a minimum fixed resolver has a private cross-target pair.
upper_bound_certificate.step_2: Choosing one private pair per query gives a graph in which each query crosses exactly its own edge; every selected edge is therefore a bridge and the graph is a forest.
upper_bound_certificate.step_3: A one-component forest would be a tree; a leaf edge forces component sizes 1 and n-1 and cannot be crossed by an exact n/2-n/2 cut.
upper_bound_certificate.step_4: For n>=6 a two-component forest is also impossible at n-2 edges: if both components are nontrivial, an edge in the smaller component cannot be crossed by an exact half cut while the larger component stays whole; if the smaller component is isolated, a leaf edge of the n-1 tree leaves a connected n-2 block larger than n/2.
upper_bound_certificate.consequence: C_F <= n-3 for every even n>=6.

sharp_construction.query_balance: Every query has exactly n/2 zeros and n/2 ones.
sharp_construction.targets: Identity targets; construction query signatures are pairwise distinct.

combined_adaptive_upper_bound: C_F <= min(m, n-3, F_2(n,C_A)) for even n>=6.
